documents.title: Outstanding invoices, balance due and overdue
documents.content: Accounts Receivable at /accounting/accounts-receivable lists every invoice that still has a balance, with the invoice date, the due date, and the balance due. The Total Outstanding card adds up those balances to the cent. An invoice shows a red days overdue badge once its due date has passed and money is still owed: an invoice due today is not overdue, and it becomes overdue the next day. Overdue is worked out from the due date and the balance each time the page opens and is never stored, so it clears the moment the invoice is paid. Paid invoices, drafts and fully covered invoices are never overdue, and a part-paid invoice can be. The client record shows the same overdue badge. An invoice that has recorded payments cannot be deleted until its payment entries are removed from the General Ledger.

documents.title: Posting a payment and issuing a receipt
documents.content: Post Payment on an invoice row opens a dialog with the payment amount, the date and the deposit account. The amount starts at the exact balance due. It must be more than zero and no more than the balance due, so an overpayment is refused with a message that names the balance, and an invoice already paid in full cannot be paid again. Posting adds the payment to the amount paid to the cent, sets the invoice Partially Paid or Paid, claims the next receipt number such as REC-20261108-001, and records the income in the General Ledger, together with this payment's share of the invoice sales tax so that tax collected is right on the Sales Tax page. The payment is reported as posted only after it has actually been saved. Choosing Post and Send Receipt opens the receipt for review, with the client email filled in, and you click Email Receipt to send it. The same checks apply when a bank transaction is matched to an invoice in reconciliation.
